record.paper_title: Open Problems in Geometric Methods for Instance-Based Learning
record.original_question: How can a nearest-neighbor decision rule be made robust when the training data contain overlapping classes or noise?

evidence.quote: How can the rule be made robust to overlapping classes or noise present in the training data?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{X} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be a feature space and let $\mathcal{Y} = \{1, 2, \ldots, c\}$ be a finite set of class labels. Suppose we are given a training sample $S = \{(x_i, y_i)\}_{i=1}^n$ drawn from an unknown joint distribution $P$ on $\mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{Y}$, where the distribution $P$ may exhibit:

(a) class overlap, meaning that there exist regions $R \subseteq \mathcal{X}$ with $P(Y = j \mid X \in R) > 0$ for more than one class $j$; and

(b) label noise, meaning that each observed label $y_i$ may differ from the true latent class $\tilde y_i$ with some unknown probability.

The standard nearest-neighbor decision rule classifies a query $x \in \mathcal{X}$ by assigning it the label of its nearest training point under a chosen metric $\rho$ on $\mathcal{X}$, namely $\hat{y}(x) = y_{i^*}$ where $i^* \in \arg\min_i \rho(x, x_i)$.

Design a modification of the nearest-neighbor decision rule (allowing, for example, weighting schemes, editing or condensing of $S$, locally adaptive metrics, $k$-NN extensions, reject options, or other geometric devices) that is provably robust to class overlap and label noise in the following sense: as $n \to \infty$, the expected misclassification probability of the modified rule converges to (or stays close to) the Bayes-optimal risk of $P$, even when a positive fraction of labels in $S$ are corrupted and the class-conditional supports overlap. Specify the rule, identify the assumptions on $P$, the noise model, and the metric under which the robustness guarantee holds, and quantify the convergence rate.
artifact.status_search_result: Numerous partial solutions exist (edited/condensed NN rules, weighted k-NN, mutual k-NN, locally adaptive metrics, prototype selection, and noise-filtering methods), each providing robustness under specific assumptions. However, a unified geometric nearest-neighbor decision rule that is provably robust to arbitrary class overlap and label noise with strong finite-sample guarantees remains an active research problem; published surveys note that performance on combined overlap-plus-noise scenarios is not yet satisfactory.

status_evidence.title: Handling class overlapping to detect noisy instances in classification
status_evidence.snippet: Class overlap and noise are major problems often associated with decreased classifier performance.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of class overlap together with label noise is recognized as a persistent challenge in instance-based classification.

status_evidence.title: Noisy data elimination using mutual k-nearest neighbor for classification mining
status_evidence.snippet: Mutual k-NN identifies pseudo nearest neighbors that are not taken into account during prediction.
status_evidence.claim: Mutual k-NN provides a partial solution by filtering noisy or non-mutual neighbors.

status_evidence.title: K-nearest neighbors rule combining prototype selection and local feature weighting
status_evidence.snippet: Combines prototype selection and local feature weighting for classification in overlapping regions.
status_evidence.claim: Local feature weighting plus prototype selection mitigates overlap, but is not a complete solution.

status_evidence.title: Effective k-nearest neighbor models for data classification enhancement
status_evidence.snippet: kNN's performance has not yet attained satisfactory levels when dealing with noisy/overlapping data.
status_evidence.claim: Recent survey indicates the problem remains only partially solved.
